Thus M and Eustathius on Dionysius Periegetes 414. The Aldine edition has χώρας [land] from a gloss, misled by which Turnebus transposed the words χώρας γὰρ ἐλθὼν Ἀπις ἐκ Ναυπακτίας [for Apis came from the land of Naupactia]. Valckenaer in Scholia on the New Testament vol. 1 p. 331 thought it should be written ἐξ ἔρας [from the land] meaning 'from the earth'. The scholiast also read πέρας [end], which he explains by πέρατος [of the end], though it is not clear how πέρα [beyond] could have been said. Eustathius p. 306, 23 derives the adverb πέραν [beyond] from πέρα [beyond]: τὸ πέρην δηλοῖ μὲν τὸ πέραν, ἔστι δὲ ἐπίρρημα μεταληφθὲν ἀπὸ θηλυκῆς αἰτιατικῆς · πέρα γὰρ [the word πέρην means πέραν, and it is an adverb taken from a feminine accusative; for πέρα]
ἡ γῆ κατὰ γλῶσσαν, ὅθεν ἡ περαία παράγεται, ἧς ἡ αἰτιατικὴ πέραν [the earth in dialect, from which περαία is derived, whose accusative is πέραν]. Compare the same author p. 84, 4 and 1475, 42.
The comparative is περαιτέρω [further], on which see.

Thus I corrected for πιμπλάντων [filling], arising from the gloss πιμπλάνων [filling] written beside περαίνων [accomplishing], about which I spoke in Fleckeisen's Annals vol. 87 p. 79. Schuetz restored the dative νος πεισιβρότῳ τε βάκτρῳ [with the staff that persuades mortals]. In M it is πισίμβροτόν τε βάκτρον [and the staff that persuades mortals].
